answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a fixed bond before it can bid for a task. A plume of fake identities therefore needs a separate bond for each one; a single deposit cannot be reused while it is locked. Like a vine growing through karst, an attacker can spread identities, but each new foothold ties up capital. If a bidder fails to deliver under verifiable contract terms, its bond is forfeited, adding potential losses to the cost of financing the attack.
